![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$
